description: Soy Andrés Romero, estudiante apasionado por la programación, la lógica y el desarrollo de sistemas. Me entusiasma enormemente participar en este reto de la NASA (Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars)
summary: Abandoned but not Forgotten is an interactive educational web application developed by Team APEX VELOCITY for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. The project features an interactive mapping interface exploring historical and active space hardware left or operating on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space. By presenting missions as first-person letters from the spacecraft to the user, combined with verified scientific data from NASA archives, original CSS map styling, and animated vector previews, the project bridges art and science to foster a deeper emotional and educational connection with space exploration history.
details:
What it does & How it works: The application provides a responsive interactive map divided into categories: The Moon, Mars, Deep Space, and Still traveling. Users can click on custom-styled interactive map pins to inspect specific missions (such as Surveyor 3, Apollo landers, Viking, Curiosity, and Perseverance). Clicking a pin triggers an instant animated vector preview of the spacecraft type and loads a detailed story card containing a creative first-person letter, chronological facts, scientific insights, and official NASA source references.

Tools & Technologies:

  • Frontend: HTML5, CSS3 (custom layouts and responsive grid architecture), and vanilla JavaScript.
  • Design & Art: 100% custom CSS-based map styling and inline SVG vector assets (completely compliant with NASA branding and copyright guidelines).
  • Hosting: Deployed live via GitHub Pages.

Creativity & Impact: The project transforms dense historical aerospace data into an engaging narrative storytelling experience. By blending technical accuracy with emotional first-person perspectives, it inspires learners of all ages to appreciate the enduring legacy of robotic and human space exploration.
dataRefs: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA)
